# Exact local planar polygonization by restoring a finite Gram matrix

This proves the contributor's proposed local construction. It does not supply a
finite decomposition of arbitrary contact sets or a global approximation
theorem for arbitrary mixed convex bodies.

## 1. Hypotheses and conclusion

Let K_z, z in a finite set P, be planar convex bodies with support functions
h_z. Fix a closed normal-angle interval I=[a,b] of length ell<pi, contained
in an open interval on which every h_z is C2 and

    r_z=h_z''+h_z >= c>0.

Suppose each of a finite list of linear support compatibility constraints
is either an equality identically on I, or has a uniform strictly positive
gap there. Assume all fixed caps have constant membership, with positive
boundary separation, on each affected compact boundary arc.

Then the portions of all fiber boundaries over I can simultaneously be
replaced by arbitrarily close polygonal arcs so that:

* every support function outside int(I) is unchanged;
* every fiber area and every specified cap area is unchanged exactly;
* all the support compatibility constraints remain valid.

Endpoint facets are allowed. The replacement preserves every linear relation
among the residual support functions, not just homothetic relations.

## 2. The positive interval energy

Let B_z solve B_z''+B_z=0 with B_z(a)=h_z(a), B_z(b)=h_z(b). Uniqueness holds
because 0<ell<pi. Put f_z=h_z-B_z, so f_z belongs to H_0^1(I). On this space

    Q(f,g)=integral_I(f'g'-fg)

is a positive definite inner product. Indeed Poincare's inequality gives
integral f'^2 >= (pi/ell)^2 integral f^2.

The cross term with B_z vanishes:

    integral_I(B_z f-B_z' f')
      =integral_I(B_z+B_z'')f-[B_z' f]_a^b=0.

Since the outside support is fixed, the global planar support-area formula
therefore gives

    area(new K_z)-area(K_z)
       =-(1/2)[Q(new f_z,new f_z)-Q(f_z,f_z)].             (1)

This global H1 formula includes endpoint curvature atoms; no untracked
endpoint-facet area is omitted.

## 3. Circumscribed support interpolation is orthogonal projection

Choose a uniform mesh a=theta_0<...<theta_N=b of spacing delta=ell/N. Let
V_delta consist of continuous functions vanishing at a,b and satisfying
v''+v=0 between consecutive nodes. Let P_delta f be its nodal interpolant.
For e=f-P_delta f and v in V_delta, integration by parts on each mesh cell
gives

    Q(e,v)=sum_cells [e v']_left^right=0,

because e vanishes at every node. Thus P_delta is the Q-orthogonal
projection. The support interpolant

    h_z^delta=B_z+P_delta f_z

is exactly the piecewise sin/cos interpolation of h_z's support values.
It is the circumscribed common-normal polygonal arc.

For a C2 function, standard interpolation estimates here follow directly
by solving e''+e=f''+f with zero endpoint values on each cell. The Green
kernel or elementary variation-of-constants formula gives, uniformly,

    ||e||_infinity=O(delta^2),
    ||e'||_infinity=O(delta).

Consequently Q(e,e)=O(delta^2). All constants are uniform over the finite
family and any fixed finite basis selected below.

## 4. Restore all required energies by a near-identity matrix

Choose a linearly independent subfamily f_1,...,f_p spanning the finite
linear span of {f_z}. Write f_z=sum_j c_zj f_j. Let

    G_ij=Q(f_i,f_j),
    G_delta,ij=Q(P_delta f_i,P_delta f_j).

Orthogonality gives

    G-G_delta=[Q((1-P_delta)f_i,(1-P_delta)f_j)]_ij >=0,
    ||G-G_delta||=O(delta^2).                             (2)

The matrix G is positive definite, so G_delta is positive definite for
sufficiently small delta. Choose

    T_delta=G^(1/2) G_delta^(-1/2).

Then T_delta G_delta T_delta^T=G and T_delta=I+O(delta^2), by continuity and
local smoothness of the positive-definite matrix square-root maps. Define

    new f_j=sum_k (T_delta)_jk P_delta f_k,
    new h_z=B_z+sum_j c_zj new f_j.                       (3)

All the original pairwise Q products are restored. In particular
Q(new f_z,new f_z)=Q(f_z,f_z), so (1) gives exact preservation of every
fiber area.

## 5. Convexity survives the matrix correction

For a C2 support function h with curvature radius r>=c, its interpolant's
interior derivative jump at a mesh node theta_j is

    m_j=[h(theta_j+delta)+h(theta_j-delta)
             -2 cos(delta)h(theta_j)]/sin(delta)
       =integral_(-delta)^delta
           [sin(delta-|u|)/sin(delta)]r(theta_j+u) du
       >=2c tan(delta/2).                                (4)

It is also O(delta), uniformly. At the left endpoint, the extra derivative
jump beyond the original right derivative is

    [h(a+delta)-h(a)cos(delta)]/sin(delta)-h'(a)
       =integral_0^delta [sin(delta-u)/sin(delta)]r(a+u)du
       >=c tan(delta/2),                                 (5)

and the right endpoint has the same lower bound. Any original endpoint
facet contributes additional nonnegative jump.

In (3), each basis function's interpolant has interior derivative jumps
O(delta), because f_j''+f_j=r_j is bounded and B_j has no jumps. Multiplying
by T_delta-I=O(delta^2) changes every interior atom by O(delta^3). Equations
(4) therefore keep every interior atom positive for small delta.

At an endpoint each interpolated f_j has bounded one-sided derivative.
The correction changes its endpoint derivative by O(delta^2). Equation
(5) supplies an O(delta) positive margin, so the gluing remains convex.
Between mesh nodes new h_z''+new h_z=0. Outside I the original curvature
measure is unchanged. Thus the complete periodic support function has
nonnegative curvature measure and is the support function of a convex body.
It remains uniformly close to the original body, and hence has interior.

## 6. Compatibility and cap volumes

If a linear relation sum_z A_z h_z=0 holds on I, it also holds for the
endpoint functions B_z, by their unique linear construction. Thus
sum_z A_z f_z=0 and sum_z A_z c_zj=0 for each basis coefficient. Formula
(3) preserves the relation exactly. This treats all active equalities.

The supports in (3) differ from the originals by O(delta^2) uniformly.
Every remaining finite constraint with a uniform positive gap therefore
survives for sufficiently small delta. Outside I nothing changes.

The changed regions converge to the original compact arcs, which have a
positive distance from each fixed cap boundary. Consequently the entire
changed region of a fiber remains either inside or outside each cap.
Its contribution to that cap's area change is either the full fiber-area
change or zero; both vanish. All prescribed cap volumes are exact.

## 7. Limits of the statement

The construction requires uniform positive curvature, a stable finite
linear equality pattern, and positive gaps for other inequalities on I.
It does not show that arbitrary attained extrema possess finitely many
such intervals. At zero curvature, matrix corrections can create negative
atoms. At contact sets accumulating inside every interval, uniform slack
can fail. Those obstructions are not removed by this local proof.
